name: INA219 current & voltage sensor
description: Texas Instruments high-side current, bus voltage and power monitor with a 12-bit ADC and an I2C interface. Measures a load's supply voltage (0-26 V) and, through a 0.1 ohm shunt, its current (up to ±3.2 A, either direction). Runs on 3-5.5 V. Sold as: INA219 breakout (6-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, VIN-, VIN+), I2C address 0x40 (0x41/0x44/0x45 with the A0/A1 jumpers).
eli5: Sits in the wire between a battery or power supply and the thing it powers, and tells your board how many volts and how much current that thing is using.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Logic supply for the INA219, 3-5.5 V (use the microcontroller's 3.3 V)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared by the logic and the circuit being measured

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up on the board)

pins.name: VIN-
pins.description: Current-sense input, load side: connect to the load's + lead. 0-26 V; never to a GPIO

pins.name: VIN+
pins.description: Current-sense input, supply side: connect to the + of the supply being measured. 0-26 V; never to a GPIO

buildNotes: The INA219 goes in series with the load: supply + to VIN+, VIN- to the load's + lead, and the supply's ground to the same GND as the microcontroller.
VIN+/VIN- may carry up to 26 V and 3.2 A: never connect them to a GPIO, and use wires thick enough for the current.
Bus voltage register 02h holds the voltage in bits 15-3 at 4 mV per count; shunt register 01h is signed at 10 uV per count. Current = shunt voltage / 0.1 ohm.
Default address 0x40; bridge A0 for 0x41, A1 for 0x44, both for 0x45 to put several on one bus.

driver.code:
# INA219 current & voltage sensor (TI INA219, SBOS448G), MicroPython driver.
# Registers are 16-bit, sent MSB first. Shunt voltage (01h): signed, LSB 10 uV.
# Bus voltage (02h): bits 15..3, LSB 4 mV (bit 1 CNVR, bit 0 OVF).
# Current is computed from the shunt voltage and the board's shunt resistor
# (0.1 ohm "R100" on the common breakouts), so no calibration register is needed.
import time

_REG_CONFIG = 0x00
_REG_SHUNT = 0x01
_REG_BUS = 0x02

# 32 V bus range, PGA /8 (+-320 mV), 12-bit shunt and bus ADC, continuous shunt + bus.
# This is the power-on default (399Fh); written explicitly in case another program changed it.
_CONFIG_DEFAULT = 0x399F


class INA219:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x40, shunt_ohms=0.1):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.shunt_ohms = shunt_ohms
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(addr, _REG_CONFIG, bytes([_CONFIG_DEFAULT >> 8, _CONFIG_DEFAULT & 0xFF]))
        time.sleep_ms(2)  # one 12-bit shunt + bus conversion takes 2 x 532 us

    def _read(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def shunt_mv(self):
        """Voltage across the shunt resistor in mV (signed, 10 uV per count)."""
        raw = self._read(_REG_SHUNT)
        if raw & 0x8000:
            raw -= 0x10000
        return raw * 0.01

    def bus_voltage(self):
        """Voltage on VIN- relative to GND, in volts (4 mV per count)."""
        return (self._read(_REG_BUS) >> 3) * 0.004

    def current_ma(self):
        """Current from VIN+ to VIN- in mA (negative if it flows the other way)."""
        return self.shunt_mv() / self.shunt_ohms

    def power_mw(self):
        """Power delivered to the load in mW."""
        return self.bus_voltage() * self.current_ma()

    def read(self):
        """Return (bus voltage in V, current in mA)."""
        return self.bus_voltage(), self.current_ma()

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ina219 import INA219

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = INA219(i2c)  # address 0x40, 0.1 ohm shunt
while True:
    v, i = sensor.read()
    print('V=%.2fV I=%.1fmA' % (v, i))
    time.sleep(1)
